title: The Evening Brief: Extreme fear grips markets as macro headwinds persist
dek: Crypto markets are deep in capitulation territory, with the Fear and Greed Index at 11 (Extreme Fear) and major assets trading sharply below their moving averages. Bitcoin spot ETFs posted outflows for a seventh consecutive day, while whale behavior shows mixed signals beneath price weakness.
author: GoCheckMyCrypto
key_fact: The desk's Fear and Greed Index stands at 11, the lowest level in 30 days, as Bitcoin remains 51.6% below its 12-month high and all major coins trade below their 200-day moving averages despite modest daily gains.
bottom_line: Crypto markets sit in Extreme Fear (Fear and Greed Index at 11) with every major asset trading sharply below trend and down 24-83% from 12-month highs. Spot Bitcoin and Ethereum ETF outflows have stretched to seven and eight consecutive days respectively, signaling retail and passive fund liquidation, while institutional whale flows tell a bifurcated story: bitcoin moving off exchanges into self-custody, but stablecoins flooding onto platforms, suggesting hedging postures ahead of ongoing volatility. The tape shows negative Bitcoin funding and stressed long positions in altcoins, typical of capitulation phases. Watch for the week ending November 28 to close to confirm whether whale accumulation persists, and monitor January 25 for Spain's new Sepblac crypto account freeze powers to take effect.
body: Crypto markets are priced in a posture of Extreme Fear. The desk's Fear and Greed Index sits at 11, the lowest reading in the past 30 days (which ranged from 10 to 51), as the market digests a broader macro environment that has pressed most major assets sharply lower over the past month.

Price action shows the depth of the selloff. Bitcoin is down 24.56% over thirty days and down 4.16% over seven days, though Bitcoin up 0.52% over 24 hours. Ether is down 27.15% over thirty days and down 4.76% over seven days, though Ether up 0.16% over 24 hours. Solana is down 30.15% over thirty days and down 4.32% over seven days, though Solana up 0.73% over 24 hours. XRP is down 28.35% over thirty days and down 3.15% over seven days, though XRP up 1.02% over 24 hours. BNB is down 25.39% over thirty days and down 4.90% over seven days, though BNB up 0.38% over 24 hours. Dogecoin is down 27.91% over thirty days and down 4.67% over seven days, though Dogecoin up 0.88% over 24 hours. Cardano is down 29.37% over thirty days and down 3.66% over seven days, though Cardano up 1.85% over 24 hours. The recovery attempts remain modest; every major asset trades below its 200-day simple moving average, with Bitcoin at 60,411 sitting 16.0% below its long-term trend line.

Technical positioning shows strain across the board. Bitcoin's RSI14 is at 27.5 (indicating potential oversold conditions), and the MACD is below its signal line; Ether's RSI14 is at 29.3 with MACD above signal; Solana's RSI14 is at 32.4 with MACD above signal. Bitcoin holds a golden cross (200-day SMA above the 50-day), as do most major altcoins, but distance from the 12-month high tells the story: Bitcoin is 51.6% below its high of $124,739.81, Ether is 64.0% below its high of $4,690.84, Solana is 69.5% below its high of $232.63, Dogecoin is 78.9% below its high of $0.2668, and Cardano is 83.1% below its high of $0.8744. Volatility remains elevated: 30-day volume swings stand at 47.7% for Bitcoin, 66.3% for Ether, 65.8% for Solana, and 73.7% for Cardano.

Spot Bitcoin ETF outflows have now run for seven consecutive days. Spot Bitcoin ETFs saw net outflows of $453.0M on the day, November 25, and spot Bitcoin ETFs saw net outflows of $2,505.6M over the week through November 25. This follows weeks of cumulative net flows on the positive side: the desk's boards show spot Bitcoin ETF cumulative net flows at $51,657.0M year-to-date, though the recent week-to-week rhythm has reversed. Ethereum ETF flows have turned more negative: Ether flows were -$68.5M on November 25, with last five sessions showing -$446.0M net; the same-direction streak is now eight days. Stablecoins continue to drain, down 5.75% over 30 days to a total supply of $282,228,143,014.

Whale and institutional behavior offers a counterpoint to the panic. Over the past 48 hours, $44,067,756 in bitcoin moved net off exchanges, a sign of accumulation or self-custody by larger holders. The desk's Whale Watch board shows $51,231,259 in bitcoin moving off Coinbase Institutional and $58,394,762 flowing into Coinbase, net of institutional demand despite price weakness. Weekly whale flows remain constructive: the week ending November 21 saw $1,615M moved off exchanges, and the week ending November 28 (the current partial window) shows $552M off exchanges so far. Stablecoin flows paint the opposite picture: net $148,784,397 in stablecoins moved onto Bitfinex over the past 48 hours, suggesting liquidity positioning ahead of potential volatility.

Leverage markets show signs of stress. Bitcoin open interest stands at $1.93B on OKX with negative funding (-0.0003% over 8 hours; -0.3% annualized), and the past 2 hours saw 100 liquidations with shorts taking $380,361 of pain versus longs at $157,886, a rough 2.4-to-1 short-to-long ratio. Ether is different: funding is positive at 0.0089% over 8 hours (9.8% annualized), open interest is $1.10B, and the 2-hour liquidation tally shows longs taking $545,309 in pain versus shorts at $38,648, a 14-to-1 long-bias squeeze. Solana and XRP show similar long liquidation pressure, with shorts facing relief.
